::: {.callout-note title="Editable submission handout"}
[Open the Explore Linux Digital Submission Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i5idpi--acAt6GjY-TNwthrjG0jv0k5VPrbG5SjVLDg/edit?usp=drivesdk). Attach it in Google Classroom and make a copy for each student when you create the assignment.

Related class materials: [Explore Linux notes](explore-linux.qmd), [Linux unit overview](index.qmd), and [Linux Start Here slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1V9VzFkTGhEyKs5TszsuZV96xya5k-zvfEx8qGKjgbzM/edit).
:::

## Learning goal

By the end of this submission:

- I will be able to show what I changed, installed, and investigated in Linux.
- I will be able to explain a few commands I used during Bashcrawl.

This is important because it enables me to show my process, not only the final result.

::: {.callout-important title="What to submit"}
Submit exactly **two files** in Google Classroom:

1. **One Google Doc** named `Explore Linux - First name - Computer name`
2. Your reviewed `linux-bash-history.txt` file

Example Google Doc name: `Explore Linux - Sam - min-tej-14`
:::

::: {.callout-danger title="Check for private information"}
Do not submit a password, Wi-Fi password, access token, student number, or other private information. Open your Bash history file and check it before attaching it.
:::

## Build your Google Doc

1. Open the Explore Linux assignment in Google Classroom.
2. Create or attach **one Google Doc**.
3. Give the Google Doc the required name.
4. Add the headings shown below.
5. Answer every required prompt.
6. Insert each screenshot directly below the matching answer.
7. Attach the reviewed Bash history text file as the second file.

## Copy these headings and prompts

### Accounts

**My Linux username:**
Write your username. Do not write your password.

**Other student 1 username:**
Write the first other student's username. Do not write the password.

**Other student 2 username:**
Write the second other student's username. Do not write the password.

**Why are the accounts different types?**
Explain why your account is an administrator account and the other two student accounts are standard accounts.

### Make Linux yours

Insert **two screenshots**:

1. The desktop before your visual change
2. The desktop after your visual change

Then answer:

- What did you change?
- Why is the desktop better for you now?
- Which three other graphical user interface (GUI) activities did you complete?

### Network check

**Connection type:**
Write Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

**Local IPv4 address:**
Write the address shown by your computer. Keep this document inside Google Classroom and do not post the address publicly.

**Did the TEJ Notes website load?**
Write Yes or No. If it did not load, explain what happened.

### Software

**Software installed:**
Write the exact name.

**What does it do?**
Explain it in one or two sentences.

**Why did you choose it?**
Explain your choice.

**Would you recommend it?**
Write Yes or No, then explain why.

### Terminal and Bashcrawl

Insert **one screenshot** that shows your Bashcrawl progress.

Then answer:

- Where did you get to in Bashcrawl?
- Which command was most useful?
- What does that command do?
- What mistake did you make, and how did you recover?
- What did `git clone` do?

### Bash history check

Write this sentence after you check the file:

`I opened my Bash history file and checked that it contains no passwords or private information.`

Attach `linux-bash-history.txt` to the Google Classroom assignment.

## Above and beyond

This section is optional, but the heading must be in your Google Doc.

If you completed only the required work, write: `I completed the required work.`

If you went further, answer the questions that apply:

- What did you do beyond the required work?
- What did you investigate, test, customize, install, or create?
- Did you try another command-line game or tutorial?
- What extra problem did you solve?
- What evidence can you show?
- What would you explore next if you had more time?

You may include one extra screenshot below this section.

## Before you turn it in

- [ ] I attached **one Google Doc**.
- [ ] I attached `linux-bash-history.txt`.
- [ ] My Google Doc name follows the required pattern.
- [ ] I answered every required prompt.
- [ ] I inserted two desktop screenshots and one Bashcrawl screenshot.
- [ ] I checked both files for passwords and private information.
- [ ] I included the **Above and beyond** heading.
- [ ] I selected **Turn in** in Google Classroom.

## Extend your learning

- Return to the [Explore Linux notes](explore-linux.qmd) or review the [Linux Start Here class slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1V9VzFkTGhEyKs5TszsuZV96xya5k-zvfEx8qGKjgbzM/edit).
- Continue [Bashcrawl](https://gitlab.com/slackermedia/bashcrawl) and see how far you can travel using only the commands the game teaches.
- Explore the school-appropriate [Learn Linux TV YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@LearnLinuxTV). Choose a beginner terminal video and try one safe command you understand.
- Try [Linux Journey](https://labex.io/linuxjourney) for free, short lessons about commands, permissions, processes, and networking.
- Try [GameShell](https://github.com/phyver/GameShell) with teacher approval when you want a longer command-line game.
- Save [OverTheWire Bandit](https://overthewire.org/wargames/bandit/) for the later Secure Shell (SSH) and networking lesson.

## Review

You created one organized Google Doc, showed your Linux changes, explained your Bashcrawl learning, and attached a safe copy of your Bash history.

## Reflect on your learning

1. Which piece of evidence best shows your learning?
2. What would make your next technical submission clearer?
